examples.label: Positive
examples.description: The pointer `base` at line 3 is overwritten at line 9 before reaching the free site at line 11. Thus there is a memory leak bug in the function goo when condition is false.

examples.label: Positive
examples.description: The pointer `base` at line 2 is not freed and doesn't escape the function foo when the function returns -1 at line 5. Thus there is a memory leak bug in the function foo when process(s) < 0.

examples.label: Negative
examples.description: There are two execution paths in the function bar. When process(s) < 0, the pointer `base` is freed at line 5. When process(s) >= 0, the pointer `base` is assigned to s->base at line 8. `s` is the function parameter propagated by the caller function, so the pointer `base` can escape the current function via pointer `s` and be freed later. Thus there is no memory leak bug in the function bar.

examples.label: Negative
examples.description: There are two execution paths in the function sample. When p == NULL, the malloc fails, no memory leak occurs. When p != NULL, the pointer `p` is assigned to x->buf at line 7. Since x is not defined in this function, we treat it as a global variable. So the pointer `base` can escape the current function and be freed later. Thus there is no memory leak bug in the function bar.
